Exercise D.S10 — Easy: Class K or class K infinity?
      
        On $r\ge0$, classify $\alpha_1(r)=2r$, $\alpha_2(r)=r^2$ and $\alpha_3(r)=r/(1+r)$ as class-$\mathcal K$ and/or class-$\mathcal K_\infty$.
        Review if needed: this section and monotonic functions.
        
          Show hint
          Class $\mathcal K$ means continuous, strictly increasing and zero at zero. Class $\mathcal K_\infty$ also requires unbounded growth.
        
        
          Show worked solution
          All three are continuous, zero at zero and strictly increasing for nonnegative arguments. For $r^2$, strict increase holds even though its derivative at zero is zero.$2r$ and $r^2$ grow without bound, so both are class-$\mathcal K_\infty$ as well as class-$\mathcal K$.$r/(1+r)$ approaches $1$, so it is class-$\mathcal K$ but not class-$\mathcal K_\infty$. The unboundedness requirement is separate from monotonicity.

Exercise D.S19 — Easy: Check a saturation sector
      
        Define $\varphi(v)=\max(-1,\min(v,1))$. Verify $0\le v\varphi(v)\le v^2$ for every real $v$. What sector does this establish?
        Review if needed: this section and Lipschitz bounds.
        
          Show hint
          Treat $|v|\le1$ and $|v|\gt1$ separately.
        
        
          Show worked solution
          If $|v|\le1$, then $\varphi(v)=v$, so $v\varphi(v)=v^2\ge0$.If $|v|\gt1$, then $\varphi(v)$ is the sign of $v$, and $v\varphi(v)=|v|$. Here $0\le|v|\le v^2$.Thus the nonlinearity lies in sector $[0,1]$: the origin-to-point slope is between $0$ and $1$. This is a pointwise statement about every input, not an estimate obtained by sampling a few values.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: For absolute input at most1 the source max/min saturation equals the input and its product is the input square, nonnegative.
hypotheses: All real inputs with absolute value<=1; endpoints included.
reviewed_clauses.reason: The definition is the literal max(-1,min(v,1)), with both boundary cases included. The actual equality and nonnegative product are proved directly.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Outside absolute input1 the saturation is the input sign and its product equals absolute input, between0 and the input square.
hypotheses: All real inputs with absolute value>1, split by their actual sign.
reviewed_clauses.reason: Both actual max/min outside branches are proved; the sign representation and true absolute-value product satisfy the stated inequalities universally.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Every real input satisfies0<=v saturation(v)<=v squared; nonzero origin-to-point quotient is between0 and1, yielding actual sector[0,1].
hypotheses: Every real input for the sector product; v!=0 only for the ordinary origin-to-point slope quotient.
reviewed_clauses.reason: The actual universal sector follows from the true global Lipschitz/monotonicity proof, and the nonzero quotient is explicitly derived using positive v squared. At zero the saturation and product are0; an undefined geometric quotient is not assigned a slope. The source sampling contrast explains this universal quantifier rather than adding an empirical claim.
